cards.text: Paul's on trial again, friend, and this time he's standing in front of King Agrippa. The king speaks first.

cards.question: King Agrippa speaks first. What does he tell Paul he has permission to do?
With King Agrippa's permission, Paul stretches out his hand and begins his defense.

cards.text: Paul's got the floor now, friend, and he looks like a man who's been waiting ALL WEEK for somebody to pass him the mic. He's defending himself against all the accusations of the Jews, and he tells King Agrippa he considers himself fortunate to stand before him today.

cards.question: Paul is defending himself against accusations from the Jews. Why is he especially glad that King Agrippa is the one hearing it?

answers.text: The king knows Jewish customs well
The king owes Paul a favor
The king has already freed him once

cards.question: Paul says the Jews have known how he's lived since his earliest childhood. He lived as a ___, in the strictest sect of their religion.
Paul gets to the charge itself. What does he tell King Agrippa he's on trial because of?

answers.text: His hope in God's promise to their fathers
His teaching against the temple in Jerusalem
His refusal to honor the laws of Rome

cards.question: Paul turns to the whole room with a question. Why would any of them consider it incredible that God ___ the dead?

cards.text: Then Paul says, "So then, I too was convinced that I ought to do all I could to oppose the name of Jesus of Nazareth." Friend, the man on trial just started reading his OWN rap sheet out loud. On purpose.

cards.question: Paul says he put many of the saints in prison in Jerusalem. When they were condemned to death, he cast his vote against them.

cards.text: He says he had the saints punished in the synagogues, and in his raging fury he went to foreign cities to persecute them. That's what he was doing on his way to Damascus, with the authority and commission of the chief priests.

cards.question: About noon, on the way to Damascus, a light from heaven brighter than the sun shines around Paul but not around his companions.

cards.text: They all fall to the ground, and Paul hears a voice speaking to him in Hebrew. All that authority from the chief priests, friend, and the man just hit the dirt like a phone off a nightstand.

cards.question: On the ground, Paul hears the voice call him by name twice. What does the voice ask him?

answers.text: Why do you run from Me

cards.question: On the Damascus road, Paul asks, "Who are You, Lord?" The Lord answers that He is ___, the one Paul is persecuting.
Jesus tells Saul to get up and stand on his feet. He has appeared to appoint Saul as a servant and a ___ of what he has seen.

cards.text: Then Jesus says He'll rescue Saul from his own people and from the Gentiles, and He's sending him to open their eyes. The man who was out to shut these people down is getting sent to open eyes, friend, and that's a CAREER CHANGE.

cards.question: Jesus is sending Saul to open people's eyes. What does Jesus want them to turn from and turn to?

answers.text: From the city to the desert

cards.text: Paul tells the king, "So then, King Agrippa, I was not disobedient to the heavenly vision." From Damascus and Jerusalem to all of Judea and then the Gentiles, he declared that people should repent and turn to God.

cards.question: As Paul preached repentance from Damascus to the Gentiles, he said people's repentance didn't need to show up in what they do.

cards.text: For this reason, Paul says, the Jews seized him in the temple courts and tried to kill him. But he's had God's help to this day, and here he stands, testifying to small and great alike.

cards.question: Paul says he's saying nothing beyond what the prophets and Moses said would happen. What did they say about the Christ?

answers.text: He would suffer and rise first from the dead
He would conquer Rome with a mighty army
He would rule forever without ever suffering

cards.question: Paul says the Christ would proclaim light only to the people of Israel.

cards.text: Right at this point in Paul's defense, Festus, the governor, cuts in. He doesn't raise his hand. He just YELLS.

cards.question: Festus cuts into Paul's defense in a loud voice: "You are ___, Paul!"
Festus shouts that something is driving Paul to madness. What does Festus blame?

cards.text: Paul answers, "I am not insane, most excellent Festus; I am speaking words of truth and sobriety." Friend, the man gets called crazy in front of a KING and still opens with MOST EXCELLENT.

cards.question: Paul tells King Agrippa that these things were done in a corner, where the king could easily have missed them.

cards.text: Then Paul asks him straight out, "King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know you do." He asked AND answered, like a text that says "You coming tonight? You're coming."

cards.question: Paul just asked King Agrippa if he believes the prophets. How does the king answer Paul?

answers.text: He asks if Paul can persuade him to become a Christian that fast
He says he gave up on the prophets long ago
He tells the guards to take Paul away right now

cards.text: Paul says, "Short time or long," and then he tells the king what he wishes to God for everyone in that room.

cards.question: King Agrippa asked if Paul could persuade him so fast. What does Paul wish to God for the king and all who hear him?

answers.text: That they would all become what he is
That they would all set him free today
That they would all judge him fairly

cards.text: Then Paul adds one exception: "except for these chains." Friend, he wants them to have everything he's got, except the jewelry.
Then the king and the governor rise, along with Bernice, who came in with the king, and everyone seated with them. When a king stands up, friend, the meeting is OVER.

cards.question: On their way out, the king and the others agree that Paul has done something worthy of imprisonment.
After hearing Paul's defense, King Agrippa tells Festus that Paul could have been released if he had not appealed to ___.

findings.problem: Stop 3, card 2 quotes "You are ___, Paul!", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The passage starts in the middle of a scene that was set up in Acts 25:23-27, but the opening card gives none of that context. It doesn't say that Festus the governor brought Paul in, that Bernice and the officials are there, or why Paul is standing before Agrippa. It also never says who King Agrippa is.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: Stop 1's only story card is flat and has no Papa Dorin voice. 'Paul's on trial again, friend... The king speaks first.' reads as plain narration, with no reaction, comparison or energy.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: Jesus's line 'It is hard for you to kick against the goads' (Acts 26:14) is never told or asked anywhere in the walkthrough. It is a key part of what Jesus says to Saul.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The card suddenly calls him 'Saul', and cards 14 and 15 keep using that name. No card ever tells the baker that Saul is Paul. Card 11 also hides the name by saying only that the voice called him by name twice.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are

findings.problem: The joke 'The man who was out to shut these people down is getting sent to open eyes' treats two groups as one. Paul persecuted the saints (Acts 26:10-11). Jesus sends him to open the eyes of his own people and the Gentiles (Acts 26:17-18). 'These people' suggests they are the same group, which the text does not say.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: Most of Jesus's commission in Acts 26:18 is never told or asked: turning 'from the power of Satan to God', receiving 'forgiveness of sins', and 'an inheritance among those sanctified by faith in Me'. Only 'open their eyes' and 'darkness to light' are covered.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The answers are not the same kind of thing. The right answer, 'From darkness to light', is a spiritual picture. Both wrong answers are geographic moves ('From the city to the desert', 'From Rome to Jerusalem'). After 'open their eyes', the right answer stands out right away.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The blank sits inside Festus's quoted words, and the card before it gives no hint of what Festus thinks of Paul. 'lying' and 'guilty' are just as believable as 'insane', so the baker can only guess the wording.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: 'still opens with MOST EXCELLENT' is not true. Paul's reply opens with 'I am not insane'. 'most excellent Festus' comes after it (Acts 26:25).

rule.text: Noticing: What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: Stop 1 covers only Acts 26:1 and has 3 cards, and then the baker gets a reveal screen for a single verse. This happens because the included sermon (Acts 26:2-23) needs its own stop and the verse before it has nowhere else to go.
findings.question: When an included sermon or parable starts one verse into the passage, should the lead-in verse get a stop of its own, be folded into the sermon's stop, or be handled some other way?

findings.problem: The card's verses field is 'Acts 25:23, Acts 26:30'. It lists an outside verse (Acts 25:23, used to say who Bernice is) as a separate reference next to the passage verse. The docs allow outside facts with their reference but don't say how a card's citation should include them.
findings.question: When a story card uses a fact from outside the passage, should its verses field include the outside reference, and if so, in what format?
